title: A Third Bank Implodes. Now What?

sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175周年，陪伴您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com斜杠subscribe上的优惠。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是每日简报。

sentences.en: On Monday morning, the federal government took over a third failing bank.
sentences.zh: 周一上午，联邦政府接管了第三家陷入困境的银行。

sentences.en: This time, First Republic.
sentences.zh: 这一次是第一共和银行。

sentences.en: Today, I speak with my colleague, Gina Smiley, about whether we're at the end of this banking crisis or the start of a new phase of financial pain.
sentences.zh: 今天，我与同事吉娜·斯迈利交谈，讨论我们是正处于这场银行危机的尾声，还是新一轮金融痛苦的开始。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月2日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Gina, another day, another bank failure.
sentences.zh: 吉娜，又是一家银行倒闭。

sentences.en: Starting to be the pattern these days.
sentences.zh: 最近这似乎成了一种模式。

sentences.en: Very much.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And after these two banks had failed, Silicon Valley Bank, then a couple days later, Signature Bank, the hope and I'd say the expectation was that this crisis might be over.
sentences.zh: 在这两家银行——硅谷银行倒闭，几天后签名银行也倒闭——之后，人们的希望，或者说预期，是这场危机可能已经结束了。

sentences.en: It was not over.
sentences.zh: 并没有结束。

sentences.en: In fact, a third bank, First Republic Bank, collapsed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，第三家银行——第一共和银行也崩溃了。

sentences.en: And it was even bigger as a bank than the previous two that failed.
sentences.zh: 而且它的规模比前两家倒闭的银行还要大。

sentences.en: So tell us about why First Republic Bank ultimately went under.
sentences.zh: 那么请给我们讲讲第一共和银行最终破产的原因。

sentences.en: I think that what happened at First Republic was sort of a slow motion reaction to what happened at Silicon Valley Bank, that first bank that failed.
sentences.zh: 我认为第一共和银行发生的事情，某种程度上是对硅谷银行那家最先倒闭的银行所发生事情的慢动作反应。

sentences.en: So Silicon Valley, as you'll remember, had planned pretty poorly for rising interest rates.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，硅谷银行对利率上升的准备非常糟糕。

sentences.en: It had to sell a bunch of investments that had lost value as interest rates rose, and that spooked customers.
sentences.zh: 随着利率上升，它不得不抛售一堆贬值的投资，这吓坏了客户。

sentences.en: So the customers pulled out their money in droves, and that really caused its probleMs.
sentences.zh: 于是客户们纷纷蜂拥提款，这确实造成了它的问题。

sentences.en: So it failed.
sentences.zh: 所以它倒闭了。

sentences.en: Signature Bank, another bank in that sort of mid-sized region, which also had, similar to Silicon Valley Bank, some exposures to interest rates,
sentences.zh: 签名银行是另一家中型区域性银行，它也和硅谷银行类似，在利率方面有一些敞口，

sentences.en: and a lot of customers over the $250,000 federal deposit insurance limit also collapsed a few days later.
sentences.zh: 并且有大量客户的存款超过了25万美元的联邦存款保险限额，几天后也崩溃了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to remind people why that $250,000 number matters, that's the point at which if you fear your bank might fail, you're very worried about that money.
sentences.zh: 为了提醒大家为什么25万美元这个数字很重要，那是如果你担心你的银行可能会倒闭，你会对这笔钱非常担忧的临界点。

sentences.en: You should pull it out is the thinking, which actually becomes a self-reinforcing cycle that leads to a run on a bank.
sentences.zh: 大家的想法是应该把钱取出来，这实际上变成了一个自我强化的循环，导致了挤兑。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: If you have deposit under $250,000 to the bank, you don't really care if the bank fails because the federal government is going to insure that.
sentences.zh: 如果你在银行的存款低于25万美元，你其实并不关心银行是否会倒闭，因为联邦政府会为此提供保险。

sentences.en: Like, your money's good.
sentences.zh: 就像你的钱很安全一样。

sentences.en: But if you're above $250,000, the federal government doesn't insure that.
sentences.zh: 但如果超过了25万美元，联邦政府就不提供保险了。

sentences.en: And so you are much more likely to look around and feel a little nervous if your bank is doing anything funny and feel like you need to run for the exits
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的银行有任何奇怪的举动，你更可能会四处张望并感到有点紧张，觉得你需要夺门而逃，

sentences.en: and make sure that money is safe.
sentences.zh: 确保这笔钱是安全的。

sentences.en: And so that's very much what we saw with these two banks.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们在这两家银行身上看到的.

sentences.en: So these first two banks fail, and then people are looking around to see who else is vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 所以前两家银行倒闭了，然后人们开始环顾四周，看还有谁是脆弱的。

sentences.en: Some investors now concerned about the health of First Republic, which also operates in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 一些投资者现在开始担心第一共和银行的健康状况，该银行也在硅谷开展业务。

sentences.en: And First Republic has a lot of shared characteristics with these other banks.
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行与这些其他银行有很多共同特征。

sentences.en: And so what we start to see is really an exodus of deposits from First Republic.
sentences.zh: 因此我们开始看到的是存款从第一共和银行的大量流失。

sentences.en: Tonight, a lifeline for First Republic.
sentences.zh: 今晚，第一共和银行迎来了救命稻草。

sentences.en: And we see the big banks try and stop that, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们看到大银行试图阻止这种情况。

sentences.en: 11 of the country's biggest banks unveiling a rescue plan to pump $30 billion in deposits to prop up the structure.
sentences.zh: 该国最大的11家银行公布了一项救援计划，注入300亿美元存款以支撑其架构。

sentences.en: And so they pull together and inject $30 billion of cash into First Republic to try and say, hey, it's safe, it's okay, it's going to make it through this period,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们齐心协力向第一共和银行注入300亿美元现金，试图告诉大家，嘿，它是安全的，没事的，它能挺过这段时期，

sentences.en: we have confidence in it.
sentences.zh: 我们对它有信心。

sentences.en: And so that basically served as a lifeline.
sentences.zh: 这基本上起到了救命稻草的作用。

sentences.en: It gave First Republic a few weeks to get back on its feet, but that, unfortunately, did not work.
sentences.zh: 它给了第一共和银行几周时间来恢复元气，但遗憾的是，这并没有奏效。

sentences.en: Tonight, we're getting our first glimpse of just how dangerously close to collapse
sentences.zh: 今晚，我们首次看到

sentences.en: First Republic Bank has come.
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行距离崩溃有多么危险的接近。

sentences.en: So Monday of last week, they disclosed that a bunch of deposits had left.
sentences.zh: 上周一，他们透露大量存款已经流失。

sentences.en: The bank revealing that customers pulled more than $100 billion in deposits during the crisis.
sentences.zh: 该银行透露，客户在危机期间提取了超过1000亿美元的存款。

sentences.en: That's a 41% drop.
sentences.zh: 这是一个41%的降幅。

sentences.en: It is a staggering number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的数字。

sentences.en: $100 billion is out the door.
sentences.zh: 1000亿美元已经流失。

sentences.en: Stock price, it just plunges all week long.
sentences.zh: 股价整周都在暴跌。

sentences.en: It seems really obvious that this bank is not going to make it.
sentences.zh: 这家银行显然撑不下去了。

sentences.en: This week, breaking news overnight, another American bank has failed.
sentences.zh: 本周，夜间突发新闻，又一家美国银行倒闭了。

sentences.en: Just this morning, financial regulators in California seized First Republic Bank.
sentences.zh: 就在今天早些时候，加州的金融监管机构接管了第一共和银行。

sentences.en: It marks the second largest bank to fail in American history.
sentences.zh: 这标志着美国历史上倒闭的第二大银行。

sentences.en: The Fed struck a deal to sell...
sentences.zh: 美联储达成了一项协议，将出售……

sentences.en: So we should think of what happened to First Republic as pretty similar to what happened to Silicon Valley Bank and to Signature Bank, but just a slower motion failure.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该认为第一共和银行的遭遇与硅谷银行和签名银行非常相似，只是倒闭的过程更慢一些。

sentences.en: It took longer, but it was more or less kind of a sin.
sentences.zh: 它花了更长时间，但或多或少是一回事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it was really sort of a chain reaction.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这确实是一种连锁反应。

sentences.en: It was the last domino to fall after Silicon Valley Bank set off the cascading dominoes.
sentences.zh: 在硅谷银行引发连环骨牌效应之后，它是倒下的最后一张骨牌。

sentences.en: But this was also a slightly different situation.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一种略有不同的情况。

sentences.en: When it came to Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, the government swooped in and backed up big depositors.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到硅谷银行和签名银行时，政府迅速介入并支持了大额存款人。

sentences.en: In the case of First Republic, the government instead immediately announced that it had arranged a shotgun marriage to JPMorgan Chase.
sentences.zh: 在第一共和银行的案例中，政府反而立即宣布已安排将其“强行嫁给”摩根大通。

sentences.en: And so by selling it off to a private buyer, the government also managed to make sure that depositors aren't going to lose their money, but it did it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过将其出售给私人买家，政府也设法确保储户不会失去他们的钱，但它是通过不同的方式做到的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And, you know, why would JPMorgan Chase want to buy a bank that is failing so badly, losing money every single day?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，为什么摩根大通会想要收购一家陷入如此深重困境、每天都在亏损的银行呢？

sentences.en: Part of it is to protect the system, right?
sentences.zh: 部分原因是为了保护系统，对吧？

sentences.en: The fact that this bank was on its last legs and that it might collapse and leave its depositors out in the cold is pretty nerve-wracking for the rest of the banking system.
sentences.zh: 这家银行已经奄奄一息，如果它倒闭并让储户陷入困境，这对于其余的银行系统来说是相当令人揪心的。

sentences.en: First Republic's a big bank, and if something goes wrong with it, you could really see sort of panic moving all through the banking system.
sentences.zh: 第一共和银行是一家大银行，如果它出了问题，你真的会看到恐慌情绪在整个银行系统中蔓延。

sentences.en: So this really staves off that possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实消除了这种可能性。

sentences.en: I think the other thing is a lot of the sort of assets on First Republic's balance sheet, a lot of its loans, a lot of its, you know, sort of business,
sentences.zh: 我认为另一件事是，第一共和银行资产负债表上的很多资产，它的许多贷款，它的许多业务，

sentences.en: isn't actually all that bad-looking.
sentences.zh: 其实看起来并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: It just didn't hold up well in the face of rising interest rates.
sentences.zh: 它只是在利率上升面前表现得不够好。

sentences.en: And JPMorgan has also, in this case, got some guarantees from the government.
sentences.zh: 而且摩根大通在这种情况下也从政府那里得到了一些担保。

sentences.en: The government is going to share in losses on the portions of the business that aren't looking so hot.
sentences.zh: 政府将分担那些看起来不太妙的业务部分的损失。

sentences.en: Now, does that mean that the government, and by that I mean you and me, the taxpayer, are now subsidizing JPMorgan Chase's purchase of First Republic?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着政府——也就是你和我，纳税人——现在在补贴摩根大通对第一共和银行的收购？

sentences.en: So far, the government has been careful to say that no taxpayer money is being used to bail out any of these failing banks.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，政府一直小心翼翼地表示，没有动用纳税人的钱来救助任何这些陷入困境的银行。

sentences.en: So is that true in this case as well?
sentences.zh: 那这种说法在这种情况下也适用吗？

sentences.en: It is, but it's a little bit complicated.
sentences.zh: 适用，但这有点复杂。

sentences.en: This deal is going to cost the government about $13 billion, which is going to be covered by the insurance fund that's paid by every federally regulated bank.
sentences.zh: 这笔交易将耗费政府约130亿美元，这笔费用将由每个受联邦监管的银行缴纳的保险基金来承担。

sentences.en: So it's not taxpayer money per se.
sentences.zh: 所以它本身并不是纳税人的钱。

sentences.en: But the banks will tell you, and some people outside of the banks will tell you, that while this is paid for by assessments on banks, at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 但银行会告诉你，银行之外的一些人也会告诉你，虽然这是通过对银行的评估来支付的，但归根结底，

sentences.en: that comes back to hit the bank customers because the banks are going to raise the money by charging more fees on mortgages, on bank accounts, on things like that.
sentences.zh: 这最终会转嫁到银行客户身上，因为银行将通过提高抵押贷款、银行账户等方面的费用来筹集资金。

sentences.en: And so it's possible that you'll still end up subsidizing this whether it's directly or not.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是否直接，你最终可能仍然会补贴这笔交易。

sentences.en: And even if you don't want to.
sentences.zh: 即使你并不想这么做。

sentences.en: So if you have any relationship with a federally regulated bank, which almost all of us do, you're in one form or another eventually helping to pay for this deal.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你与任何受联邦监管的银行有任何业务往来（我们几乎所有人都有），你最终都在以某种形式帮助支付这笔交易。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So if you're JPMorgan Chase, this is a pretty good deal, obviously, but there's something a little bit funny about it, which is that JPMorgan Chase
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是摩根大通，这显然是一笔相当不错的交易，但其中有一点怪异之处，那就是摩根大通

sentences.en: is already the nation's largest bank.
sentences.zh: 已经是全国最大的银行了。

sentences.en: And after the financial crisis in 2008, the whole idea was that big banks shouldn't get any bigger, shouldn't be buying up their rivals because they might become too big to fail.
sentences.zh: 在2008年金融危机之后，整个理念是大银行不应该变得更大，不应该收购竞争对手，因为它们可能会变得“大到不能倒”。

sentences.en: So this deal seemed kind of at odds with that.
sentences.zh: 所以这笔交易似乎与这种理念有些矛盾。

sentences.en: So it is a little weird.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实有点奇怪。

sentences.en: I think the message we all took from 2008 was that really big banks can be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从2008年吸取的教训是，真正的大银行可能是危险的。

sentences.en: And certainly that was baked into the legislation that we saw passing after 2008.
sentences.zh: 当然，这已经融入了我们在2008年之后通过的立法中。

sentences.en: We saw a restriction that said the largest banks in America can no longer acquire really big banks because we don't want too much of the nation's deposit base
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一条限制规定，即美国最大的银行不再能够收购真正的大银行，因为我们不希望全国过多的存款基础

sentences.en: concentrated at any one bank.
sentences.zh: 集中在任何一家银行。

sentences.en: However, there was an exception to that rule.
sentences.zh: 然而，该规则有一个例外。

sentences.en: And the exception is that if a bank is failing, a large bank can acquire it.
sentences.zh: 这个例外是，如果一家银行正在倒闭，大银行可以收购它。

sentences.en: And that's really what we saw come into play here.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们在本案中看到发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: J.P.
sentences.zh: 摩根大通

sentences.en: Morgan was also able to offer the least-cost option to acquire First Republic and the government's required to take the least-cost option.
sentences.zh: 也能够提供收购第一共和银行的最低成本方案，而政府被要求选择最低成本方案。

sentences.en: And so ultimately, because of the exception, because of the cost calculus, it was the bank that was chosen to take over First Republic.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终由于例外情况，由于成本计算，它成为了被选中接管第一共和银行的银行。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So if this sounds like something that violates the 2008 principles, it's because it did, but those 2008 principles had a little exception clause
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这听起来像是一件违反2008年原则的事情，那是因为它的确违反了，但那些2008年的原则有一个小小的例外条款，

sentences.en: and the situation just happens to fit it.
sentences.zh: 而当前的情况恰好符合它。

sentences.en: We had an asterisk.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个星号。

sentences.en: This is the asterisk.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个星号。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, while we're on the subject of 2008, the Times published data over the past couple of days that kind of blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，在2008年的话题上，《时报》在过去几天发布的数据让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: It found that during this latest banking crisis, the banks that have failed so far held more assets than all of the banks that collapsed in 2008
sentences.zh: 它发现，在最近这次银行危机中，迄今为止倒闭的银行所持有的资产，比2008年全球金融危机顶峰时期

sentences.en: at the height of the global financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 所有倒闭银行的总和还要多。

sentences.en: So given how costly this crisis has already become, three bank failures into it, I wonder if we've now achieved a better understanding
sentences.zh: 鉴于这场危机在经历了三家银行倒闭后已经变得如此代价高昂，我想知道我们现在是否对谁对最近这次危机负有最大责任，

sentences.en: of who is most responsible for this latest crisis and whether it's the banks or the regulators.
sentences.zh: 以及到底是银行还是监管机构，有了更好的理解。

sentences.en: So these failures have been really big.
sentences.zh: 这些倒闭事件确实规模巨大。

sentences.en: At the same time, it's not 2008.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，现在不是2008年。

sentences.en: It's not clear that we're at the start of some sort of cascading financial crisis like we were back then.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚我们是否像当年那样正处于某种连锁金融危机的开端。

sentences.en: There hasn't been the same kind of risk-taking, we don't think.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，并没有出现那种程度的风险承担。

sentences.en: We're not seeing that kind of interconnected disaster.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到那种相互关联的灾难。

sentences.en: But it is clear that something went wrong here, that something allowed these risks, these banks to sort of grow out of control to a point where they could crash like this.
sentences.zh: 但显然这里出了问题，某种原因让这些风险、这些银行失控增长，达到了可以这样崩溃的地步。

sentences.en: So the government has started to take a look into what exactly that something was.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府已经开始调查这“某种原因”究竟是什么。

sentences.en: And we saw their first pass at that last week.
sentences.zh: 上周我们看到了他们对此的初步尝试。

sentences.en: They released some autopsies into what happened at Silicon Valley Bank and at Signature Bank.
sentences.zh: 他们发布了一些关于硅谷银行和签名银行发生事件的调查报告。

sentences.en: Who dropped the ball?
sentences.zh: 是谁失职了？

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the upshot from those is the government really took a finger and pointed it right back at themselves.
sentences.zh: 这些报告的结论是，政府实际上把矛头直接指向了自己。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，把DJ台

sentences.en: into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成这样一个充满美丽50年历史文物的生动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在您喜爱的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Winna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘温娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了游戏《Connections》，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个拼图。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都在制作 Spelling Bee 和 Letterboxd 这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联色觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到那些声音的主人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: So, Gina, why do these government autopsies point a finger so strongly right back at the regulators themselves?
sentences.zh: 吉娜，为什么这些政府调查报告会把矛头如此直白地指向监管机构本身？

sentences.en: So we have these couple of reports that come out last week.
sentences.zh: 我们上周看到了几份这样的报告。

sentences.en: And the one that I thought was really interesting was this report that the Federal Reserve put out on Silicon Valley Bank.
sentences.zh: 其中令我最感兴趣的是美联储发布的关于硅谷银行的这份报告。

sentences.en: This thing is hundreds of pages long.
sentences.zh: 这份东西长达数百页。

sentences.en: It's a ton of documents about what went wrong with this bank's oversight, what regulators were seeing in real time, what supervisors were saying.
sentences.zh: 里面包含大量文件，记录了这家银行的监管哪里出了问题、监管机构当时看到了什么、监督人员当时是怎么说的。

sentences.en: And a lot of this report sort of harkens back to a set of changes that you've discussed on the show before, which is there were some pretty important
sentences.zh: 而且这篇报告很大程度上让人回想起你以前在节目中讨论过的一系列变革，也就是有一些相当重要的

sentences.en: regulatory rollbacks that happened in 2018 and 2019 that allowed banks to get a lot bigger before they were subject to the government's strictest, both regulations and supervision,
sentences.zh: 监管放松政策在2018年和2019年出台，这让银行在达到政府最严格的监管和监督（也就是日常监管）标准之前，可以变得规模大得多。

sentences.en: so day-to-day oversight.
sentences.zh: 也就是日常监督。

sentences.en: And Silicon Valley Bank was growing pretty rapidly in the years leading up to these reforMs.
sentences.zh: 在这些改革出台前的几年里，硅谷银行的增长速度相当快。

sentences.en: And because of them, it didn't move up into sort of big bank oversight, which tends to be a bit more strenuous, a bit more professionalized,
sentences.zh: 正因为这些改革，它没有被归入那种通常更严格、更专业化的大银行监管范畴，

sentences.en: just a little bit more intensive all around until a few years later than it otherwise would have.
sentences.zh: 也就是在各方面都更深入一些，直到比原本应该的时间晚了好几年才被归入。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Before these regulatory rollbacks,
sentences.zh: 在这些监管放松之前，

sentences.en: Silicon Valley Bank would have been supervised more strictly earlier, faster, with less money under management.
sentences.zh: 硅谷银行会在管理资金较少的时候，更早、更快地受到更严格的监管。

sentences.en: But after these rollbacks, it just took longer.
sentences.zh: 但在这些放松政策出台后，这个过程变慢了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that mattered because some risks were able to sort of grow and metastasize and get worse without a lot of intervention.
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为有些风险在缺乏大量干预的情况下得以滋生、扩散并恶化。

sentences.en: And by the time they were recognized, it was pretty late in the game.
sentences.zh: 等它们被识别出来时，已经为时已晚了。

sentences.en: And what were some of the things these supervisors finally did find?
sentences.zh: 这些监督人员最终到底发现了什么？

sentences.en: So the regulators, the supervisors, start really noticing that management has some pretty bad risk management practices.
sentences.zh: 监管机构和监督人员开始真正注意到，管理层有一些相当糟糕的风险管理做法。

sentences.en: They're really not minding their liquidity risk.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有放在心上流动性风险。

sentences.en: And that means that they're just not keeping sort of a good enough cushion in the case that something might go wrong.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在可能出问题的情况下，他们没有留出足够的缓冲资金。

sentences.en: But despite all of these findings, they're not really cracking down on this bank all that hard.
sentences.zh: 但尽管发现了所有这些问题，他们并没有对这家银行采取特别严厉的打击措施。

sentences.en: You know, what we saw was that they gave them a decent score on liquidity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们看到的是，他们在流动性方面给出了一个还不错的评分。

sentences.en: Again, that financial cushion component of this, even after they had recognized some of this pretty significant risk-taking.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这就是财务缓冲的那部分，即便在他们已经认识到这种相当显著的风险承担之后也是如此。

sentences.en: And how do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: I mean, what is it that this report finds
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这份报告发现是什么

sentences.en: animates that decision to say everything's okay or to let it slide when it looks problematic?
sentences.zh: 促成了这种决定：当事情看起来有问题时，却说一切正常或者对此听之任之？

sentences.en: So this is alluded to a little bit in the report, but my reporting has also shown, I think in a little bit more depth, that it's pretty clearly the case that the supervisors
sentences.zh: 报告中对此有一点暗示，但我的采访也显示，可能更加深入一点，很明显的情况是，

sentences.en: who are overseeing these institutions felt like you really couldn't crack down on an institution the first year that it moved up into this stricter oversight regime.
sentences.zh: 监督这些机构的主管们觉得，在一家机构刚进入这种更严格监管制度的第一年，你实在无法对其实施严厉打击。

sentences.en: And so the delay that had happened earlier just kind of cascaded through this bank's whole story and really resulted in, even as recently as 2022,
sentences.zh: 因此，早期发生的延误就像滚雪球一样贯穿了这家银行的整个故事，并最终导致——甚至在最近的2022年，

sentences.en: when it's really starting to get its wrist slapped for the first time, a pretty gentle oversight regime that allowed a lot of problems to go unresolved.
sentences.zh: 当它第一次真正开始受到警告时——依然是一个相当宽松的监管制度，导致许多问题长期得不到解决。

sentences.en: So what you're describing is a crucial set of years
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的是一段关键的岁月，

sentences.en: where Silicon Valley Bank doesn't get regulated in the way it would have if these laws hadn't been rolled back.
sentences.zh: 在这期间，硅谷银行没有按照如果这些法律没有被放松本应有的方式接受监管。

sentences.en: And then once it does get regulated, the culture of people inside the Fed is to not be too hard on the new guy, the new big bank.
sentences.zh: 而一旦它真正受到监管，美联储内部人员的文化就是不要对新人、新大行太严苛。

sentences.en: And so taking this all together, there's kind of, you know, a missed opportunity in these two or three years to nip serious problems in the bud at Silicon Valley Bank.
sentences.zh: 所以综合来看，在硅谷银行萌芽严重问题的那两三年里，可以说是错失良机。

sentences.en: Things went too slow.
sentences.zh: 事情进展得太慢了。

sentences.en: There was also just simply some plain old misdiagnosis that happened here.
sentences.zh: 这里面也确实存在一些简单粗暴的误诊。

sentences.en: So for example, one of the interesting documents showed that in the middle of 2021, some of the supervisors watching over Silicon Valley Bank were worried about the possibility
sentences.zh: 例如，一份有趣的文件显示，在2021年中期，一些监督硅谷银行的主管曾担心这样一种可能性：

sentences.en: that they weren't properly protected in the case that interest rates fell, that interest rates went down.
sentences.zh: 即在利率下跌、利率下降的情况下，他们没有受到适当的保护。

sentences.en: Which is interesting because by the middle of 2021, inflation had started to pick up.
sentences.zh: 这就很有意思了，因为到2021年中期，通货膨胀已经开始抬头。

sentences.en: And so increasingly, the risk by that point was that interest rates would increase, which we saw them do in 2022.
sentences.zh: 因此，到那个时候，风险日益变成了利率上升，我们在2022年也确实看到了这种情况。

sentences.en: You know, the Federal Reserve, within a few months of that, had started raising interest rates.
sentences.zh: 你知道，美联储在那之后的几个月内就开始加息了。

sentences.en: And so not only was the bank not properly prepared for that, but it seems like maybe the supervisors weren't aware that they needed to be taking that risk into account.
sentences.zh: 因此，不仅银行没有为此做好充分准备，而且看起来监管机构似乎也没有意识到他们需要把这种风险考虑在内。

sentences.en: Wrong risk, as it turned out.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，押错了风险。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So I think what happened here was sort of this cocktail of actual regulatory changes, a fairly lax supervisory culture, and just plain old, you know, boring mistakes.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里发生的事情是实际监管政策的调整、相当松懈的监督文化，以及一些简单、陈旧、无聊的失误共同发酵的结果。

sentences.en: Which you're saying when they're finally all brought together in this cocktail ultimately lead to Silicon Valley Bank having so much risk that it fails and that that failure
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，当这些因素最终汇聚在一起时，最终导致硅谷银行背负了如此巨大的风险以至于倒闭，而这次倒闭

sentences.en: brings us to where we are right now, which is the failure not just of Silicon Valley Bank, but of Signature and now of First Republic.
sentences.zh: 把我们带到了当前的境地，不仅是硅谷银行倒闭，Signature 银行和现在的第一共和银行也相继倒闭。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But ultimately, Gina, these banks, the three of them that we've been talking about, made decisions that caused their own failures.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，吉娜，我们一直在谈论的这三家银行，是它们自己做出的决定导致了自身的倒闭。

sentences.en: And one of the common threads for all three of them was that they were focused on customers, depositors, who had a lot of money to put in these banks.
sentences.zh: 这三家银行的共同点之一，就是它们都专注于那些在这些银行存有大量资金的客户和储户。

sentences.en: And because they had so much money in the bank, that put the whole bank at a higher risk of a bank run because these people worried that anything over $250,000
sentences.zh: 正因为他们在银行里有如此多的资金，这使得整家银行面临更高的挤兑风险，因为这些人担心任何超过 25 万美元的资金

sentences.en: wasn't going to be insured by the federal government.
sentences.zh: 都不会受到联邦政府的保险保障。

sentences.en: So I wonder if these banks could have on their own really lowered their risk of being in the situation they're now in by just having a more balanced group of clients
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，如果这些银行能像大银行那样拥有更均衡的客户群体，它们本可以靠自己真正降低陷入目前这种境地的风险。

sentences.en: the way that the big banks do.
sentences.zh: 就像大银行那样。

sentences.en: You know, people with a lot less money could be their customers too.
sentences.zh: 你知道，资金少得多的人也可以成为它们的客户。

sentences.en: You know, I think anytime you have a bank failure, you have clearly had a failure of bank management.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为每当发生银行倒闭时，显然都说明银行管理层出现了失职。

sentences.en: Like, bank managers are supposed to make sure that their banks aren't vulnerable to failing.
sentences.zh: 比如，银行管理者本该确保他们的银行不会脆弱到倒闭的地步。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, what you just explained is really a situation of sort of concentrated risk.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，你刚刚解释的实际上是一种集中风险的情况。

sentences.en: There's nothing wrong with having big customers.
sentences.zh: 拥有大客户并没有错。

sentences.en: There's nothing wrong with having uninsured deposits.
sentences.zh: 拥有未保险存款并没有错。

sentences.en: The problem is when you don't have enough of a variety of customers, when you're not thinking about making sure that you're balancing all of your risk, which is what happened
sentences.zh: 问题在于当你没有足够多样的客户时，当你没有考虑确保平衡所有风险时——这正是在硅谷银行身上发生的事情。

sentences.en: particularly in the case of Silicon Valley Bank.
sentences.zh: 硅谷银行尤其如此。

sentences.en: And those kinds of problems, those sort of gaping vulnerabilities are the kinds of things that regulation is supposed to catch.
sentences.zh: 而那种类型的问题，那种明显的脆弱性，正是监管本应捕捉到的东西。

sentences.en: So I've spent a lot of time talking about this with my sources over recent weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以我最近几周花了很多时间跟我的消息源讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: And I'll often say, you know,
sentences.zh: 我经常会说，

sentences.en: I'm getting told that a lot of this was the fault of the managers.
sentences.zh: 我听说这很大程度上是管理层的责任。

sentences.en: And they will say back to me, of course it was the fault of the managers.
sentences.zh: 而他们会反问我，这当然是管理层的责任。

sentences.en: But this is why we have regulation.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么我们要设立监管。

sentences.en: Regulation is supposed to step in where CEOs fail.
sentences.zh: 当 CEO 们失败时，监管本应介入。

sentences.en: And there's a reason we do this to banks in particular, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对银行采取这种特殊对待是有原因的，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, we don't regulate everything like this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不会对所有事情都进行这样的监管。

sentences.en: Your local toy store is not regulated the way a bank would be regulated.
sentences.zh: 你家门口的玩具店可不会像银行那样受到监管。

sentences.en: It's because these banks are the beating heart of the center of our economy.
sentences.zh: 那是因为这些银行是我们经济中心跳动的心脏。

sentences.en: They have such big knock-on effects when something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 当它们出问题时，会产生巨大的连锁反应。

sentences.en: And so we, as a nation, as sort of a society, have decided that it's really important to make sure that we're keeping an eye on these folks.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一个国家、作为一个社会，我们认为确保密切关注这些机构是非常重要的。

sentences.en: Gina, where do we now go from here?
sentences.zh: 吉娜，我们接下来该何去何从？

sentences.en: Because this now feels like a crisis that in terms of dollars is significant.
sentences.zh: 因为现在这感觉像是一场在资金规模上很显著的危机。

sentences.en: We talked about that.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: And yet it's oddly contained as banking crises go.
sentences.zh: 然而，就银行业危机而言，它的范围又被诡异地控制住了。

sentences.en: And perhaps that's because these are regional banks and lots and lots of people were untouched by these collapses.
sentences.zh: 也许这是因为它们是区域性银行，成千上万的人没有受到这些倒闭事件的影响。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: 2008 touched everybody because it was so interconnected with the entire economy, as you said.
sentences.zh: 2008年的危机波及了所有人，因为它与整个经济紧密相连，正如你所说的那样。

sentences.en: But if you bank at Bank of America or Wells Fargo or Chase right now, what happened at these three banks doesn't really affect you that much.
sentences.zh: 但如果你现在在美国银行、富国银行或大通银行有账户，这三家银行发生的事并不会对你产生太大影响。

sentences.en: And it kind of feels like we might now be at the end of whatever this set of dominoes was, right?
sentences.zh: 而且感觉我们现在可能已经走到了这一系列多米诺骨牌的尽头，对吧？

sentences.en: Is that how you see this?
sentences.zh: 你是这么看的吗？

sentences.en: I think that's the optimistic take is that this could be the end of it, stick a fork in it, we're past this.
sentences.zh: 我认为比较乐观的看法是，这可能是这一切的终点，大局已定，我们已经熬过去了。

sentences.en: I think there's a more nuanced take, one that an economist described to me this morning, which is that we might be past the acute phase of this situation.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一种更微妙的看法，一位经济学家今天早上向我描述过，那就是我们可能已经度过了这场危机的急性期。

sentences.en: You know, the bank failures that we were going to see in response to SVB are now behind us, but we might be moving into the chronic phase.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们因应对硅谷银行事件而要经历的银行倒闭潮现在已经抛在身后了，但我们可能正在进入慢性期。

sentences.en: And the chronic phase here has a lot to do with the interest rate increases we've seen over the last year and a half.
sentences.zh: 这里的慢性期与我们过去一年半见证的加息密切相关。

sentences.en: When interest rates go up, it tends to displace other parts of financial markets.
sentences.zh: 当利率上升时，往往会冲击金融市场的其他部分。

sentences.en: It tends to sort of show us where the weaknesses are.
sentences.zh: 它往往会向我们展示薄弱环节在哪里。

sentences.en: We pretty clearly saw that in the case of these banks.
sentences.zh: 我们在这些银行身上非常清楚地看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: Silicon Valley Bank was very exposed to rising interest rates in a way that it hadn't handled well, and that's a big portion of why it failed.
sentences.zh: 硅谷银行对利率上升非常敏感，却没有妥善处理，这是它倒闭的很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: And so, the Fed is set to meet on Wednesday and it's expected to raise interest rates again.
sentences.zh: 因此，美联储定于周三开会，预计将再次加息。

sentences.en: That might be its last interest rate increase in this cycle.
sentences.zh: 这可能是它在这个周期中的最后一次加息。

sentences.en: They've suggested that they might hit pause after that.
sentences.zh: 他们已经暗示之后可能会暂停加息。

sentences.en: We don't know for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们还不能百分之百确定。

sentences.en: But regardless, rates are a lot higher than they've been in a really long time, and we could have more weaknesses out there that we just haven't recognized yet.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，利率比很长一段时间以来的水平都要高得多，我们可能还有更多尚未被发现的薄弱环节。

sentences.en: You know, there's this phrase that you often hear in finance, which is when interest rates rise, the tide goes out and you see who's swimming naked.
sentences.zh: 你知道，金融界经常听到这样一句话：当利率上升时，退潮了才知道谁在裸泳。

sentences.en: And I think we've seen a couple of the people who are swimming naked, but the tide's not all the way out yet.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经看到了一些裸泳的人，但还没有完全退潮。

sentences.en: So, we might still see more to come.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可能还会看到更多状况出现。

sentences.en: There may be additional vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 可能还会有其他的脆弱性暴露出来。

sentences.en: More naked banks.
sentences.zh: 更多的裸泳银行。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 好的，

sentences.en: Gina, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 吉娜，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们深表感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的权力争斗之中。
